column_semantics: For debt investments, the schedule has Reference Rate (2), Spread (2), and Interest Rate (2). PIK is printed as a component inside Spread (2), while Interest Rate (2) prints the all-in total rate including the reference rate, cash spread, and PIK component. For equity/preferred-style rows, the schedule uses All-In Rate and prints 100% PIK directly in that all-in rate cell.

rationale: The printed debt schedule does not label the InvestmentInterestRate column as cash-only. Instead, it separates the additive rate mechanics: Reference Rate (2), Spread (2), and Interest Rate (2). Actual PIK rows show the cash spread and PIK component in the Spread (2) cell, while the Interest Rate (2) cell is the total rate, e.g. Ellkay shows SOFR, spread '3.25 %, 3.50 % PIK', and interest rate '10.98 %'; Espresso shows SOFR, spread '2.63 %, 3.13 % PIK', and interest rate '9.75 %'. Equity/preferred-style rows use an explicit All-In Rate column and print '10.50 % ( 100 % PIK)' for Integrity Marketing Group.
